review_notes: Reviewed all 177 lines, the transport definitions, relevant Mathlib simp rules, and related scalar-normalization proofs. One missing canonical simp rule is supported by repeated uses. No Lean execution was performed.

findings.excerpt:
have he (t : Time) : interpolation θ' t = q⁻¹ • interpolation θ t :=
    Measure.map_smul _ (continuous_eval_const t).measurable.aemeasurable
findings.problem: Scalar compatibility of interpolation is only available as a specialized local fact. The canonical reduction `interpolation (c • π) t` to `c • interpolation π t` consequently requires explicit measurability arguments and unfolding here, again in hξend and hs', and in related proofs. Mathlib's conditional simp rule Measure.map_smul supplies the underlying equality but does not expose an unconditional interface for interpolation.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp] lemma interpolation_smul (c : ℝ≥0∞) (π : Measure (Curve X)) (t : Time) : interpolation (c • π) t = c • interpolation π t`, proved using `Measure.map_smul c (continuous_eval_const t).measurable.aemeasurable`. Replace the local he and map-level scalar conversions with this rule. Register only the scalar-outward direction; use its reverse explicitly where cancellation requires it.
findings.benefit: Normalization and rescaling proofs can retain the interpolation abstraction without repeatedly supplying measurability. The orientation removes a scalar from beneath interpolation without expanding its definition. It holds for zero and infinite scalars too; the separate nonzero and finiteness assumptions remain necessary for cancellation.

def interpolation (π : Measure (Curve X)) (t : Time) : Measure X :=
  Measure.map (fun γ : Curve X => γ t) π

protected theorem map_smul {R : Type*} [SMul R ℝ≥0∞] [IsScalarTower R ℝ≥0∞ ℝ≥0∞]
    (c : R) {μ : Measure α} {f : α → β} (hf : AEMeasurable f μ) : (c • μ).map f = c • μ.map f := by
